title: Spectral probability at a fixed level
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the Boolean cube $\\{-1,1\\}^n$, and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. The probability that a spectral sample of $f$ has exactly $k$ elements equals the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients of the real-valued version of $f$ over all coordinate subsets of cardinality $k$.
